message_1_subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology
message_1_body:
Jordan,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Below is a short recap of what we discussed, the primary pain points you called out, and proposed next steps for a focused POC.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: Tail latency spikes on embeddings and chat generation during peak business hours (observed 95th percentile ~1.2s for short queries, but 99th spikes as high as 3.8s).
- Goal: Stable 95th %-tile latency <= 350ms for typical user prompts and 99th %-tile <= 800ms, while maintaining throughput of ~120 reqs/sec average with 400 reqs/sec burst capability.
- Model constraints: Need to support a 32k-context model for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) flows and smaller 4k models for lower-cost routes.
- Compliance: Data residency in us-west, audit logs retained 1 year.

What we recommend (high-level)
- Deployment: Start with Redwood Dedicated in us-west for predictable throughput; enable automatic fallback to hosted variants for burst handling.
- Model strategy: Serve a 32k-context large model for RAG-critical endpoints and a quantized 4k model variant for lower-cost traffic and canary rollouts.
- Runtime optimizations: KV-prefix caching for repeated RAG prefixes, continuous batching with a small latency SLO-aware batch window (10–30ms), and selective quantization for smaller models.
- Network/topology: Co-locate retrieval nodes and inference GPUs in same VPC to avoid extra hop latency; see attached network diagram.

Action items
- Redwood: Share SLO matrix + recommended config + network diagram (attached).
- Acme: Confirm expected steady-state QPS and peak burst window, and share any internal egress/firewall constraints.
- Schedule: POC kickoff — propose Mon May 3 10:00am PT (I put a tentative invite; confirm if that works).

Attachments: redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx, acme-network-diagram.png

Thanks,
Marissa

message_3_subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology — proposed config
message_3_body:
Jordan,

Thanks for the details — great signal. Short answer: you can meet the 95th/99th SLO targets with Dedicated + caching, but achieving those numbers consistently for the 32k model requires careful placement and some headroom.

Proposed tech specifics
- Capacity: Dedicated GPU pool (4 x A100 equivalent) pinned for inference with autoscale for short bursts to 12 GPUs using warm instances. This covers slow KV-hit misses and long RAG queries.
- Memory/Model: Host 32k-context model on multi-GPU sharded instances (tensor-parallel) to fit the KV cache and large attention memory. Quantized 4k variants (4-bit) for the low-cost route.
- Batching: Use a small dynamic batching window (10–30ms) for chat/embeddings to keep tail low; for long RAG requests route to a separate queue with an expanded batch window and higher CPU memory allowance.
- KV caching: Prefix KV cache for RAG rounds; expected cache hit rate 35–50% depending on query locality which reduces effective compute and latency on repeated reads.
- Network: Co-located retrieval nodes + Redis cache within same VPC/subnet and private peering to avoid public egress. TLS termination at the edge is fine; keep model-to-retrieval hops <1ms.
- Instrumentation: Per-route token-level tracing, 95/99/latency histograms, and alerting on regression vs baseline. We'll push an SLO dashboard during the POC.

Attachments: redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx (detailed numbers), acme-network-diagram.png, poc-deploy-playbook.md (attached as text in repo).

I'll be available in the kickoff to run through the topology and help size the initial Dedicated pool.

—Connor
